newsitem.title: UK: Britain to build replacement for Royal Yacht.
newsitem.headline: Britain to build replacement for Royal Yacht.

text.p: The British government will build a replacement in British shipyards for the Royal Yacht Britannia, Defence Secretary Michael Portillo told parliament on Wednesday.

"We have taken that decision because we believe that a Royal Yacht is an important national asset and projects a prestigious image of Britain which adds powerfully to official occasions and to British economic interests," he said. The cost will be about 60 million pounds ($99.42 million), he added. ($1=.6035 Pound)

Britannia, used by Queen Elizabeth when making state visits, is to be decommissioned towards the end of 1997 after 44 years afloat. It sailed on Monday on its final voyage to Hong Kong for the ceremonial handover of the colony to China on June 30.

The sleek 6,000 tonne luxury mini-liner costs about 10 million pounds a year to run, but advocates of its replacement say it is a unique asset that has helped to secure two billion pounds of exports for Britain over the past decade.

Portillo said Britannia's replacement would be paid for by the nation, not by private finance, but the Queen would contribute to the new yacht's furnishings and fittings. The running costs should be about half of Britannia's, he added.
"Britain can look forward to a Royal Yacht in the new century. I trust she will enter service in time for Her Majesty's Golden Jubilee in 2002," Portillo said.
